hello.note: General hello for any time of day. In casual speech many speakers open instead with Kedụ? ('how are you/what's up'), and Nnọọ ('welcome') is reserved for greeting someone arriving, not for hailing someone in passing.

goodbye.note: Literally 'until later/next time'; the standard parting phrase, distinct from Kedu (hello).

how_are_you.note: The short form Kedụ? ('how?') alone is the everyday casual opener among peers, closer to 'what's up' than a full inquiry.

youre_welcome.note: The same word used to welcome an arriving guest, reused as the standard reply to thank you.

no_problem.note: Literally 'there is no trouble'; casual reassurance, distinct from the more formal Nnọọ reply.

excuse_me.note: Literally 'please wait'; used to politely interrupt, get attention, or ask someone to make way.

sorry.note: Also used to express sympathy, not just apology.

of_course.note: Literally 'truly/indeed'; used as an emphatic yes.

cheers.note: Literally 'let's drink'; Igbo has no single dedicated toast word, and many speakers just say Cheers in English.
